name: Shubham Panwar
project: Women-Led Sustainable Mushroom Cultivation for Nutrition and Livelihood in Rural Uttarkashi
place: Jhala, Harsil Valley and Saini, Dunda block, Uttarkashi
deck: Forty women in two Uttarkashi villages, four hundred kilos of straw that would otherwise have been burnt, and seventy kilos of mushrooms out of the first cycle at Saini. Temperature and humidity tracked over WhatsApp.
description: Forty women, two units, four hundred kilos of straw that was not burnt, and seventy kilos of mushrooms from the first cycle in an Uttarkashi winter.

aims.p: Straw, spawn, a sealing machine, a weighing machine and printed packaging in each village. Enough to sell from, not only to grow in.
The straw becomes a mushroom bed or it becomes smoke. Four hundred kilos went the first way.

aims.h: Sell to the road that is already there
aims.p: Sixteen to seventeen lakh people a year travel the Gangotri route past these villages. The packaging exists for them.

did: Surveyed both villages and mobilised forty women across eight self-help groups
Ran hands-on training in Jhala and in Saini on cultivation, hygiene, packaging and basic marketing
Set up two women-managed units, each with 200 kg of straw, twenty spawn packets and sealing and weighing machines
Moved spawn up the valley by refrigerated trailer
Tracked temperature and humidity through a WhatsApp group across the first production cycle

frames.alt: A line of women in headscarves and long skirts standing across a stony hillside yard, each holding a bulky sack of pale straw substrate against her chest, a heap of filled sacks on a blue tarpaulin on the ground in front of them and a bare-branched tree and steep Himalayan slopes behind

quotes.text: Ab hum ghar baithe hi income kar sakte hain aur parivar ko nutritious khana bhi de sakte hain.
quotes.speaker: Sangeeta Devi

quotes.text: Jhala mein itni thand mein bhi mushroom ug aaya — yeh bahut badi baat hai.
quotes.speaker: Abhishek Rauntela
